openUiAnatomy: no published Open UI text-input anatomy — union of salt-ds Input (NOT multiline/number/pill/formatted/tokenized/search-input), shadcn Input (new-york-v4), and M3 filled-text-field + outlined-text-field (one component, two emphasis variants — the same treatment button's filled/outlined/text family got). The label + help-text wrapper is a SEPARATE canonical component (`field` / Salt `form-field`) and is not modelled here; only how Salt's Input reads state out of form-field context is recorded, as behavior.status-inheritance. See docs/INPUT-MATRIX.md scope note.

behavior.pattern: a native single-line text control. Caret, IME, selection and autofill are platform-owned in all three systems. The cross-system axes are: WHERE the chrome lives (a wrapper element vs the input element itself), WHICH mechanism draws the edge (a bottom-only activation indicator vs a full box border), how focus is expressed (dotted outline / translucent ring / thicker indicator), and how wide the validation-status enum is (3 / 1 / 1).
behavior.chassis: skeleton/input.tsx — written from the template's part union (root box, control, activation indicator, start/end adornment containers, automatic status adornment); inherits from no design system. The root/control split is a config axis, not a fixed DOM: when chrome="control" the wrapper is display:contents and the <input> itself carries every box style, as it does in shadcn.

rows.note: WHERE the chrome lives, and it is real structure, not a DOM-shape convenience. Salt and M3 need a wrapper: adornments and an activation indicator have to sit inside the box beside the text (Salt: <div class="saltInput"> around <input class="saltInput-input">, plus .saltInput-activationIndicator and the adornment containers). shadcn does NOT: input.tsx renders a bare <input data-slot="input"> and nothing else, so its border/background/padding/radius/height/shadow all sit on the input element itself. Every box-level style row's selector below unions BOTH vocabularies ([data-chrome="wrapper"] on the root, [data-chrome="control"] descending to the control), and the skeleton gives the wrapper display:contents when chrome="control" so shadcn's rendered box model really is a single element. Wrapping shadcn in a styled div would have been the box-model equivalent of the tooltip's one-rotated-square arrow — invisible in a screenshot, wrong in source.

The edge mechanism, and a genuine two-way structural split — NOT one bordered box with a colour delta. "underline" is a bottom-only rule that thickens on focus; "box" is a full border on all four sides. THE SURPRISE, straight from source: Salt's DEFAULT is underline, not box. Input.css renders .saltInput-activationIndicator unconditionally and `bordered` defaults to false, so an out-of-the-box Salt input is an underline that goes 1px -> 2px on focus — the identical mechanism AND the identical numbers as M3's filled-text-field (active-indicator-height 1px -> focus-active-indicator-height 2px). Salt's box border is the opt-in (`bordered={true}`, which zeroes the indicator). So the real alignment is Salt-default + M3-filled = underline, versus Salt-bordered + shadcn + M3-outlined = box. shadcn has no underline mechanism at all.

Salt: `startAdornment` prop -> .saltInput-startAdornmentContainer (padding-right spacing-100, column-gap spacing-100, and dedicated size overrides for composed Buttons). M3: leading-icon-size 24px + leading-icon-color + with-leading-content-leading-space. shadcn: OFF — the bare input has no adornment slot; adornments are the separate `input-group` component (docs/COMPONENTS.md), out of scope here.
Salt: `endAdornment` prop. M3: trailing-icon-size 24px + trailing-icon-color (and error-trailing-icon-color). shadcn: OFF, same reason as the start adornment.

An AUTOMATIC validation glyph the component inserts itself — Salt only: `{!isDisabled && validationStatus && <StatusAdornment status={validationStatus} />}`. M3 is OFF for a precise reason: it defines error-trailing-icon-color, i.e. it RECOLOURS a trailing icon in the error state, but never inserts one — the glyph is always consumer-supplied content. shadcn has no icon concept on input at all. DECLARED COMPOSITION: which glyph renders, and its own fill, belong to Salt's StatusAdornment/semantic-icon-provider — a future registry icon component; only size, placement and colour source are modelled here.

shared invariant: all three render a native single-line <input>. Caret movement, text selection, IME composition, autofill and clipboard are platform-owned and identical — nothing to switch per column.

HOW each system knows it is focused, and it is not the same mechanism. Salt: React state — useState(focused) with onFocus/onBlur handlers on the <input>, applied as a .saltInput-focused CLASS on the WRAPPER (not :focus-within, not :focus-visible; and onFocus is not even attached when disabled). shadcn: the native :focus-visible pseudo-class, no JS. M3: [R], no live component in the tokens-only clone. This skeleton reproduces Salt's mechanism (React focus state -> a data-focused attribute on the root) because it is the only one of the three that works identically for both chrome values; for a text input :focus-visible matches on pointer focus too, so the rendered result matches shadcn as well. Declared.

DECLARED COMPOSITION with the separate `field` component (docs/COMPONENTS.md's field row = Salt's form-field). Salt only: useFormFieldProps() supplies disabled, readOnly, necessity and validationStatus plus a11yProps (aria-labelledby/aria-describedby, merged with the instance's own). The precedence is NOT uniform and is worth recording exactly: isDisabled = disabled || formFieldDisabled and isReadOnly = readOnlyProp || formFieldReadOnly (OR — either source can switch it on), but validationStatus = formFieldValidationStatus ?? validationStatusProp (the CONTEXT WINS OUTRIGHT over the instance prop). shadcn has no context channel at all — its Field marks itself data-invalid and the input's own aria-invalid is set per instance. M3: [R].

Salt only: an empty read-only Input renders the literal em-dash "—" in place of the value (emptyReadOnlyMarker prop, default "—"; passing '' disables it). This is CONTENT FORMATTING, not CSS — exactly the class of character CALENDAR-MATRIX.md's post-mortem found the deleted pilot had silently lost, so it is a first-class config row rather than a footnote. shadcn and M3 have no equivalent.

Salt writes tabIndex={isDisabled ? -1 : 0} onto the input explicitly, overriding the native default, and omits the onFocus handler entirely while disabled. shadcn relies on the native disabled attribute plus disabled:pointer-events-none. M3: [R]. Same capability, two different levels of explicitness.

The background-intensity axis. Salt: "primary" | "secondary" | "tertiary", default "primary"; each class reassigns --input-background / --input-background-disabled to editable-{variant}-background (snow / marble / limestone in light). shadcn: OFF, no such axis. M3: OFF as a SEPARATE axis — M3's only variant axis is filled-vs-outlined, which is already modelled as structure.indicator; recording it here as well would invent a second axis M3 does not have and would leave the two toggles able to contradict each other.

Coverage is 3 / 1 / 1. Salt: error | warning | success — and note that `info` is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, because Input takes FormFieldValidationStatus, which is literally Omit<ValidationStatuses,"info"> (Salt's Banner and Tooltip both DO accept info; one design system, two status enums for two of its own components). shadcn: a single boolean, aria-invalid — error only, no warning, no success, the same tone-coverage gap already recorded for Button and Alert. M3: a single error-* token family; direct grep of both text-field files finds no warning or success token anywhere.

Salt only: "left" | "center" | "right", default "left", applied as an inline --input-textAlign custom property that .saltInput-input reads. Discriminated by the theme-invariant [data-text-align="…"] rules in this template's base block (text-align is genuinely theme-invariant, so it belongs there rather than in a per-column cell). shadcn and M3 have no equivalent prop.

All three. Discriminated by four separate style rows below (background/colour/border/indicator) plus style.control.disabled — and the three systems answer it with three different mechanisms: Salt retokenises each colour to a 40%-alpha sibling, shadcn drops one blanket opacity:0.5 over the whole element, M3 layers FOUR different per-element opacities (container 4%, outline 12%, indicator 38%, text 38%) over the enabled colours.

Salt: a real prop WITH a dedicated visual state (its own background, border colour and cursor). shadcn: the native attribute works and the skeleton sets it (so the control genuinely becomes non-editable), but there is NO visual state — input.tsx has no read-only: variant and the docs page has Disabled and Invalid sections with no read-only section at all. That non-variation is sourced, not a missing cell, so the shadcn read-only instance in the harness renders identically to rest BY DESIGN. M3: OFF — no read-only token in either text-field file.
consumer-owned value and placeholder text in all three.

consumer-owned content, where the system has the part. Salt accepts any ReactNode and gives composed Buttons dedicated overrides (--saltButton-height: calc(size-base - spacing-100), --saltButton-borderRadius: palette-corner-weaker, negative margins to bleed to the box edge); M3 expects a 24px icon; shadcn has no slot.
same as slot.start-adornment, on the trailing side.

DECLARED COMPOSITION (the pattern calendar.template.json's slot.composes established). Three compositions are deliberately NOT reimplemented here: (a) the `field` wrapper — label, help text, necessity marker, and Salt's whole form-field context channel — a separate canonical component; (b) `button`, for Salt's adornment buttons and shadcn's input-group buttons; (c) an icon set, for the status adornment glyph and any leading/trailing icons. All three render as neutral placeholders in this skeleton rather than importing another component's skeleton, keeping this build self-contained; their own matrices will replace the approximations.

Rest and focus exist in all three. HOVER DOES NOT: shadcn's input has no hover: class of any kind — every class in input.tsx was read, this is a confirmed absence, not an unfound value. Salt recolours border/indicator to palette-accent on hover; M3 recolours to on-surface. shadcn's input does not react to the pointer at all until it is focused.
all three; see prop.disabled for the three different mechanisms.

a distinct VISUAL state in Salt only. Salt's read-only background is `transparent` (editable-background-readonly -> color-transparent), so a read-only input dissolves into the page; its border/indicator go to palette-neutral-readonly (gray-500 at 10% alpha). Its cursor token --salt-cursor-readonly resolves to `text`, the SAME value as --salt-cursor-text — a tokenised distinction with no visual consequence, recorded here rather than given a row of its own.

see prop.validation-status. Worth recording separately: M3 is the only system whose HOVER colour in the error state is a different role from its rest colour in the error state (error-hover-active-indicator-color / error-hover-outline-color both resolve to on-error-container, not error).

shown at each system's default (Salt variant=primary, M3 filled). Every column aliases the same indirection slot name, `bg-current`, which the variant/status rows below reassign — mirroring Salt's own --input-background mechanism.

M3 only, and it is the outlined variant's defining difference: _md-comp-outlined-text-field.scss has NO container-color token at all (direct grep — contrast filled's), so an outlined field is transparent. Salt is OFF because `bordered` changes the border and nothing else — a real non-variation. shadcn is OFF because box is its only mode.

the control inherits this (base gives [data-slot="input-control"] color:inherit), matching Salt, where .saltInput sets the colour and .saltInput-input inherits it. shadcn is the honest outlier: input.tsx sets NO text-colour class, so this is the ambient --foreground, recorded as such rather than presented as a component token.

Salt: --salt-text-* body role by density; Input.css sets family/size/line-height but NOT weight, so the 400 in this shorthand is the ambient --salt-text-fontWeight (regular), recorded not invented. shadcn: text-base md:text-sm — the value here is the >=768px one (0.875rem/1.25rem); see the DECLARED GENERATOR GAP in the column provenance and INPUT-MATRIX.md finding 9, since this generator has no @media channel. M3: body-large (1rem/1.5rem, weight-regular), Roboto self-hosted per this pipeline's standing M3 precedent.

a separate row from style.root.font because the CSS `font` shorthand does not carry letter-spacing. Salt: --salt-text-letterSpacing = 0, declared explicitly in Input.css. shadcn: OFF — no tracking utility on the element. M3: body-large-tracking = 0.03125rem.

Salt sets both height and min-height to --salt-size-base (20/28/36/44 by density). shadcn: h-9 = 36px, density-invariant (shadcn has no density capability — foundations/density.md). M3: container-height 56px, which arrives in the `latest` edition already stamped @deprecated and does not exist at all in v0.192 — the only sourced height number in either edition, recorded with that caveat rather than replaced by a guess.

Salt: 4em, the hardcoded --saltInput-minWidth default fallback. Checked against TOOLTIP-MATRIX.md's frozen-token lesson and kept as a literal: it is em-relative, so it already scales with the density-driven font size, unlike a bare px literal would. shadcn: min-w-0 = 0. M3: OFF, no width token.

Salt: padding-left/right = spacing-100 and NO vertical padding at all — height alone sets the vertical rhythm. shadcn: py-1 px-3 = 4px 12px. M3: 16px uniform (top/bottom/leading/trailing-space from tokens/_md-comp-{filled,outlined}-field.scss, a declared cross-edition borrow — see the Edition pin in INPUT-MATRIX.md); 16 + 24 (body-large line-height) + 16 reproduces the 56px container height exactly.

the space between the box's edge content (adornments, status glyph) and the text. ONE row covers both of Salt's gaps because they are the same token: the adornment containers' padding-right/padding-left AND their internal column-gap are all --salt-spacing-100, as is StatusAdornment's padding-left. M3: content-space = 16px. shadcn: OFF, it has no adornments (and no wrapper for a gap to live on).

Salt: palette-corner-weak -> curve-100 (rounded edition pin, same as Button/Tooltip) = 2/4/6/8px by density. shadcn: rounded-md -> --radius-md = 0.625rem * 0.8 = 8px. M3 filled: corner-extra-small-TOP = `4px 4px 0 0` — rounded on the top only, so the activation indicator sits on a square bottom edge. That asymmetry is the filled variant's signature and is why it is a four-value radius, not a single number.

M3 only: the outlined variant is corner-extra-small = 4px on ALL FOUR corners, since it has no bottom indicator to sit flat on. Salt is OFF — its corner is independent of `bordered`. shadcn is OFF — box is its only mode, already covered by style.root.shape.

Salt only, and explicitly tokenised: .saltInput:hover { cursor: var(--salt-cursor-text) }. shadcn and M3 declare no cursor at rest and inherit the native <input> default — recorded as an absence, not as an inherited value.

shadcn only: shadow-xs. Same value already extracted for button.shadcn.json's style.root.elevation, reused rather than re-derived. Salt has no box-shadow anywhere in Input.css (the same total absence TOOLTIP-MATRIX.md found on Salt's tooltip motion); M3 has no elevation token in either text-field file.

shadcn only: transition-[color,box-shadow] — the PROPERTY LIST is sourced [S], but no duration or easing utility is present, so Tailwind's own defaults apply and Tailwind is not vendored in this clone. 150ms / cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) are therefore [R], the same unvendored-package caveat TOOLTIP-MATRIX.md recorded for tw-animate-css. Salt: no transition/animation rule exists in Input.css at all. M3: no motion token in either text-field file.

All three style the placeholder, but only Salt changes its WEIGHT: --salt-text-fontWeight-small -> fontWeight-light = 300, alongside content-secondary-foreground. DECLARED RENDERING APPROXIMATION: this repo self-hosts Open Sans at 400 and 600 only (fonts/), so a 300 request resolves to the 400 face — the sourced 300 is kept in the cell (source truth) and the shortfall is declared rather than the value being quietly rounded. shadcn: placeholder:text-muted-foreground, colour only. M3: input-text-placeholder-color -> on-surface-variant, colour only.

M3 only — the only system that tokenises the text cursor's colour (caret-color -> primary, and error-focus-caret-color -> error, which the status row below reassigns). Salt and shadcn both leave the caret to the platform. A one-cell row, but exactly the kind of detail a 'close enough' shared chassis silently drops.

the full four-sided border. All three have one (Salt only when bordered={true}), and all three read it through the same `border-current` indirection slot so a single status reassignment recolours the border, its hover/focus variants and — in Salt's case — the activation indicator and the status glyph too.

the bottom-only activation indicator — a SEPARATE MECHANISM from the box border above, not a colour delta on it. Salt: 1px solid, reading the same --input-borderColor indirection as its box border. M3 filled: active-indicator-height 1px, active-indicator-color -> on-surface-variant, which is a DIFFERENT sys-color role from the outlined variant's `outline`. shadcn: OFF — no underline mechanism of any kind.

Salt: recolour only, to editable-borderColor-hover (palette-accent). M3: recolour to on-surface; hover-outline-width stays 1px. shadcn: OFF, and this is a CONFIRMED ABSENCE — every class in input.tsx was read and there is no hover: rule of any kind; a shadcn input does not react to the pointer until it is focused.
Salt: --input-borderColor-hover (accent). M3: hover-active-indicator-color -> on-surface. shadcn: OFF.

Salt: recolour to editable-borderColor-active (palette-accent-stronger), width unchanged. shadcn: recolour to --ring (focus-visible:border-ring), width unchanged. M3 outlined: recolour to primary AND thicken to 3px (focus-outline-width) — 2px in v0.192, the single substantive value divergence between the two M3 editions.

A real convergence, arrived at independently: Salt thickens the indicator to --salt-size-fixed-200 = 2px and recolours to accent-stronger; M3 thickens to focus-active-indicator-height = 2px and recolours to primary. Same mechanism, same number. shadcn: OFF.

Salt only, and an easily-missed source detail modelled rather than dropped: Input.css zeroes the activation indicator whenever `bordered` — EXCEPT when also focused, where .saltInput-bordered.saltInput-focused .saltInput-activationIndicator brings it back at --salt-size-fixed-100 = 1px on top of the box border. M3's outlined field has no indicator at all; shadcn has none either.

a genuine three-way structural split for 'how does focus read'. Salt: a 2px DOTTED OUTLINE outside the box (focused-outlineWidth=size-fixed-200, focused-outlineStyle=borderStyle-dotted, focused-outlineColor=palette-accent-stronger), IN ADDITION to the border/indicator recolour above. shadcn: outline:none plus a 3px TRANSLUCENT RING drawn as a box-shadow (ring-[3px] ring-ring/50). M3: OFF — nothing extra at all; focus is expressed entirely by the indicator/outline thickening and recolouring. M3's focus-indicator-outline-* tokens do exist but carry an explicit '@deprecated — instead use focus outline tokens' annotation, so this is a sourced off, not an unfound value.

Salt only: editable-background-readonly -> color-transparent, so a read-only Salt input dissolves into the page. Reads the bg-current-readonly indirection, which the status rows also reassign (Salt tints a read-only input with the status background). shadcn and M3 are OFF — a sourced non-variation and a missing token respectively, not gaps in extraction.
Salt only: editable-borderColor-readonly -> palette-neutral-readonly -> gray-500 at 10% alpha, mode-invariant.
Salt only, same palette-neutral-readonly value as the box border.

Salt: editable-primary-background-disabled, i.e. the 40%-alpha sibling of the enabled background, reassigned per variant by the variant rows. M3: on-surface at 4% (disabled-container-opacity). shadcn: OFF — one blanket opacity:0.5 does the whole job instead (see style.control.disabled).

M3 only, and a precision row rather than a new mechanism: disabled-container-opacity (4%) is a FILLED-variant token — _md-comp-outlined-text-field.scss has no disabled-container-color and no container-color at all — so an outlined M3 field must stay transparent when disabled. Without this row the shared style.root.background@disabled rule would tint it, inventing a value source does not have. Salt is OFF because its disabled background is indicator-independent; shadcn is OFF because it has no disabled background at all.
Salt: content-primary-foreground-disabled (black/white at 40% alpha). M3: on-surface at 38% (disabled-input-text-opacity). shadcn: OFF, opacity again.

Salt: editable-borderColor-disabled -> palette-neutral-disabled (gray-500 at 40% alpha), mode-invariant. M3: on-surface at 12% (disabled-outline-opacity) — note M3 uses a DIFFERENT opacity for the outline (12%) than for the indicator (38%) or the text (38%). shadcn: OFF.
Salt: the same palette-neutral-disabled as its box border. M3: on-surface at 38% (disabled-active-indicator-opacity) — three times the outline's 12%. shadcn: OFF.

the non-colour part of disabled. Salt: cursor:not-allowed (--salt-cursor-disabled). shadcn: opacity:0.5 + cursor:not-allowed + pointer-events:none — and because shadcn's control IS its box, that one opacity dims border, background and text together, which is precisely why its four colour rows above are OFF. M3: OFF, its disabled treatment is entirely per-element opacity baked into the colour rows.

DECLARED COMPOSITION: Salt's number here is not an icon size, it is Salt sizing a composed Button inside the adornment container — --saltButton-height: calc(var(--salt-size-base) - var(--salt-spacing-100)), i.e. 16/20/24/28px by density. M3's is a real icon token (leading-icon-size / trailing-icon-size = 24px). shadcn: OFF, no adornments.

Salt only: StatusAdornment.css height/min-height = --salt-size-adornment = 6/8/10/12px by density. Checked against TOOLTIP-MATRIX.md's frozen-token lesson — this is the row that would most plausibly have been a bare literal, and it is not: it is already a density token in source.

Salt only. Aliased to the SAME border-current indirection the box/indicator read, because in source they resolve to the identical value: StatusAdornment's --statusAdornment-color -> status-{s}-foreground-decorative -> palette-{negative,warning,positive}, and Input's --input-borderColor -> status-{s}-borderColor -> the same palette-{role} token. One indirection, three consumers — the same reuse ALERT-MATRIX.md's tone-active slot made for border + icon.

Salt only. Reassigns the background indirection exactly as .saltInput-secondary does (--input-background / --input-background-disabled -> editable-secondary-*), rather than duplicating the background rows. shadcn and M3 have no such axis.
Salt only — see style.root.variant@secondary.

Modelled as an indirection reassignment because that is literally what every source does. Salt's .saltInput-error sets SIX custom properties in one block (--input-background, --input-background-readonly, --input-borderColor, --input-borderColor-active, --input-borderColor-hover, --input-outlineColor) which eleven separate rules elsewhere in Input.css consume; duplicating that as per-property overrides would have meant ~30 rows. shadcn reassigns border + focus-border to --destructive AND changes the focus ring's ALPHA from 50% to 20% light / 40% dark (aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20 dark:aria-invalid:ring-destructive/40) — modelled with a ring-alpha slot so the mode split stays in the slots block where it belongs. M3 reassigns outline, outline-hover, outline-focus, indicator, indicator-hover, indicator-focus and the caret; note its hover colour in the error state is on-error-container, a DIFFERENT role from its rest colour.

Salt only — palette-warning / warning-weakest. shadcn has NO warning state at all (its status axis is the single aria-invalid boolean) and M3 has no warning token in either text-field file: the same tone-coverage gap already recorded for Button and Alert, now confirmed a third time.
Salt only — palette-positive / positive-weakest. shadcn and M3: no success state, see style.root.status@warning.
